newsitem.title: USA: Federal program to accept more white women.
newsitem.headline: Federal program to accept more white women.

text.p: The Small Business Administration will greatly expand the number of white women eligible for a federal programme that aids minority businesses, SBA Administrator Aida Alvarez said.

In an interview published in Wednesday editions of the Washington Post, Alvarez said new regulations for the SBA's 8(a) minority business programme will add several thousand new firms, with the lion's share of the increase to come from firms owned by white women.

In fiscal 1996, about 6,000 firms received $6.4 billion in federal contracts through the programme, which permits federal agencies to reserve contracts for minority-owned firms. But in 1994, only nine of the firms were owned by white women, nine by white males, and nine others by whites with disabilities, the newspaper said.
The new rules would make it easier for white women to contend that they had been subject to discrimination in the contracting market, SBA officials told the paper.
